interfaces.name: Web application
interfaces.classification_rationale: Actions are expressed by manipulating views, controls and menus over a persistent, navigable representation of file state.

provenance.evidence: Official developer documentation footer links Dropbox Web as the service client.

interfaces.name: Desktop application
interfaces.technology: First-party desktop GUI client for Windows, macOS and Linux
interfaces.classification_rationale: Persistent GUI client whose interaction is affordance manipulation; one logical interface across platforms sharing the same contract.

provenance.evidence: Official 'Desktop app' link on the developer documentation.

interfaces.name: Mobile application
interfaces.classification_rationale: Interaction through affordance manipulation on mobile screens.

provenance.evidence: Official 'Mobile app' link on the developer documentation.

interfaces.name: Dropbox API (HTTP/RPC v2)
interfaces.technology: HTTP API with RPC, content and upload endpoints under OAuth 2.0
interfaces.classification_rationale: The consumer explicitly invokes provider-defined operations through structured HTTP requests; one interface across resource groups under a shared base and auth.

provenance.evidence: Official docs describe an API for developers to work with files, including full-text search, thumbnails and sharing.

interfaces.name: Linux desktop CLI (dropbox command)
interfaces.technology: Command-line interface controlling the desktop daemon
interfaces.classification_rationale: Consumer invokes provider-defined structured commands (start, stop, status, ls, sharelink); command-based, no navigable TUI.

provenance.evidence: Official help center documents that the desktop app can be controlled with the Linux CLI and lists its commands.

interfaces.name: Webhooks
interfaces.technology: Outbound HTTP notifications to a registered receiver URI
interfaces.classification_rationale: The service initiates an HTTP request to a consumer-controlled URI whenever files in connected accounts change.

provenance.evidence: Official webhooks guide: Dropbox sends an HTTP request to the registered URI on every change in connected accounts.

access_mechanism_ledger.detail: Linux CLI is command-based only; no persistent navigable TUI documented.
Client wrapper over the HTTP API, explicitly stated to be not a formally supported Dropbox product.
Embeddable developer integration widgets, not standalone access channels; would be Interactive if counted, a channel already observed.
Extension point to launch third-party apps from a file; part of the web/desktop UI, not a distinct access channel.
Provides AI access to the API documentation, not to the Dropbox service.
Documentation help assistant, not a service access channel.
Third-party integrations, not first-party access mechanisms.
Separate product (dash.dropbox.com), out of scope for the core Dropbox service.
